question:
**Direction: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.**

Mr. Ahirwar disowned his son as he was found to be **__indulged in burglary__**.
solution:
The correct answer is **"involved in stealing."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original phrase **"indulged in burglary"** is not grammatically incorrect, but using "involved in stealing" makes the sentence more concise and clear.
 
• **"Involved"** is a better verb choice than **"indulged"** because it implies that the son was not just participating in burglary, but was actively engaged in it.
 
• **"Stealing"** is a more specific term than **"burglary," **which could refer to a variety of crimes committed in someone's home or business.
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Rustling"** refers specifically to stealing livestock, so it is not an appropriate term for this sentence.
 
• **"Smuggling"** refers to the illegal transportation of goods across borders, which does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• **"Sneaking"** implies a more covert and secretive type of theft, which may not accurately describe the son's actions.
